Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 1:

Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim (In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful)

Tafsir Surat al-Naml (Commentary on the Chapter of the Ant)

It is Meccan.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Ta Sin﴾ We have already explained its meaning in the preceding surah.

And His saying: ﴿These are the verses of the Qur'an﴾, meaning: these are the verses of the Qur'an.

﴿And a Book﴾, meaning: and the verses of a manifest Book. As for the derivation of "Qur'an" and "Kitab" (Book), we have already explained it. The scholars of the meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: The verses are made manifest at one time by recitation and at another time by writing; so the verses are made manifest by being a Book, and by being a Qur'an.

Almighty Allah's saying: ﴿Guidance and good tidings for the believers﴾. That is: guidance from misguidance, and good tidings of reward, which is Paradise. It is also said: the verses are guiding and bringing good tidings.

And His saying: ﴿for the believers﴾ means: for those who affirm (the truth).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 3:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Those who establish the prayer﴾. The establishment of the prayer (iqamat al-salat) is performing it with its obligatory parts (fara'id) and its sunnah practices. It is also said: the establishment of the prayer is guarding its appointed times (mawaqit).

And His saying: (and who give the zakat). That is: they give the zakat. Zakat is the zakat on wealth. It is also said: it is the zakat of fitr (zakat al-fitr).

And His saying: (and in the Hereafter they are certain). That is: they believe in it (yusaddiqun).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 4:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter – We have made their deeds appealing to them﴾. The majority of scholars hold that these are deeds of disobedience. It has also been said: they are acts of obedience, and this is by establishing proof of their goodness.

And His words: ﴿so they wander blindly﴾, that is, they are bewildered and hesitant, and it is said: they are blind (ya'mūn).

Allah's saying: ﴿Those are the ones for whom is the worst of punishment﴾ means: its most severe (form).

And His saying: ﴿and in the Hereafter they are the greatest losers﴾ means: in share and portion.

Allah's words: ﴿And indeed, you are receiving the Qur'an from One who is All-Wise, All-Knowing﴾. That is, you are being given the Qur'an. It is also said: you are taking the Qur'an. And it is also said: you are being taught the Qur'an.

As for His words: ﴿from One who is All-Wise, All-Knowing﴾, that is, from His presence.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 7:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿When Moses said to his family, "Indeed, I have perceived a fire"﴾. That is, "I saw a fire." From this comes the word *ins* (humankind), they were named *ins* because they are seen and see (*mar'iyyun mubsirun*).

In the narrative, Moses had lost his way. Some have mentioned that Moses, peace be upon him, was tending his sheep on the edge of the valley, and the sheep saw the fire and were frightened and scattered, and Moses did not see it. So Moses called out to the sheep until they gathered, then they scattered again, and he called out to them until they gathered, then they scattered a third time. Moses looked and saw the fire, so Moses, peace be upon him, went seeking it.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿I will bring you from it some news﴾. That is, news about the way.

And His saying: ﴿Or I will bring you a burning brand (*shihab qabas*)﴾. It was read with tanwin (*shihabin qabasin*), and it was also read as an idafa (construct): *shihabu qabasin*. The words *shihab* and *qabas* are close in meaning. A stick that has fire at one of its ends, and no fire at the other end, is called *shihab*, and it is also called *qabas*. Some have said: *shihab* is something luminous like a pillar, and the Arabs call every white thing that has light a *shihab*. *Qabas* is a piece of fire. The poet said:

(In his hand is a straight, well-shaped spear,
for it there is a point like the flame of a firebrand.)

As for the reading with tanwin, *qabas* is treated as an adjective (*na't*) for *shihab*. As for the reading with idafa, it is the idafa of a thing to itself, like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the Abode of the Hereafter﴾, and like the saying of people: "the day of Friday," and what is similar to that.

His saying: ﴿So that you may warm yourselves﴾. In it is evidence that they were in a cold night, and that the cold had reached him. The Arabs say: "Come to the *salá* (warmth of fire) and the *qirá* (hospitality)."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 8:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So when he came to it, he was called: "Blessed is whoever is in the fire"﴾. The people of tafsir (exegesis) said: What he saw was not a fire, but light. He called it fire only because fire is never free of light; and because it appeared to Musa to be fire.

As for His saying ﴿whoever is in the fire﴾, there are several opinions. Most of the exegetes hold that it is the Light of the Lord, and this is the view of Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and others. Abu Bakr al-Hudhali reported from al-Hasan al-Basri that it is Allah, the Exalted. Al-Farra' mentioned that "whoever is in the fire" refers to the angels, and "whoever is around it" are also the angels (according to the first opinion, "whoever is around it" are also the angels).

There is a fourth view regarding this verse, namely that "whoever is in the fire" refers to Musa. If it is said: Musa was not in the fire. We reply: He was near the fire, and the Arabs call one who is near a thing "in" it. They say: When you reach Dhat 'Irq, you are in Makkah, meaning because of its nearness to Makkah. Musa was near the fire, so He made him as if he were in the fire.

There is a fifth view regarding this verse, namely that "min" (whoever) means "ma" (what), and the meaning of the verse is: Blessed is the fire and what is around it. Some of them mentioned that in the reading of Ubayy it is: "Blessed is the fire and whoever is around it." The Arabs say: "Barakallah," "Barakallahu 'alayka," and "Buriku fika" with one meaning.

As for His saying ﴿And glorified is Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾, He declared Himself free of every imperfection, and He is the one free of every evil and defect.

Qur'anic quotation: ﴿O Musa, indeed it is I, Allah, the All-Mighty, the All-Wise﴾. That is: indeed I am Allah, the All-Mighty, the All-Wise. Al-Farra' said: the hā' (in innahu) is an ʿimād (a dummy or supporting pronoun) in this position.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 10:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And throw down your staff.﴾ Then when he saw it moving (tahtazz), ﴿as if it were a jann,﴾ meaning: moving (tataharrak).

His saying: ﴿As if it were a jann.﴾ The jann is the small snake that is much given to agitation (idtirab). We have already explained the reconciliation (tawfiq) between this verse and His saying: ﴿Then behold, it was a manifest serpent (thu'ban mubin).﴾

His saying: ﴿He turned back, fleeing (mudbiran).﴾ That is: he ran away. It is also said: he returned along the way by which he had come.

His saying: ﴿And did not look back (wa lam yu'aqqib).﴾ That is: he did not turn around.

His saying: ﴿O Moses, do not fear.﴾ (In some of the tafsirs: when Moses was startled and fled, God, may He be exalted, said to him: ﴿Come forward,﴾ but he did not return. So He said: ﴿Do not fear,﴾ [for] indeed you are among the secure ones.) He did not return, so He said: ﴿We shall restore it to its former state (sirataha al-ula).﴾ He still did not return until He made it a staff as it had been. Then he returned and took it. And God knows best.

His saying: ﴿Indeed, the messengers do not fear in My presence.﴾ That is: when I have made them secure. It is also said: they do not fear punishment from Me, for I do not punish them.

If it is said: Did not all the prophets fear God, and did not the Prophet fear God, and did he not say: "I am the most fearful of you (ana akhshakum)"? The answer to this is: the fear that is a condition of faith is obligatory and cannot be free of anyone, whereas this fear is fear of punishment for disbelief and major sins, and God, may He be exalted, has preserved the prophets from disbelief and major sins.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 11:

As for His saying: ﴿except for the one who wrongs﴾, there are several opinions regarding it. The first: "Nor the one who wrongs," ﴿then substitutes good after evil﴾, meaning: he repents and feels remorse. This view is weak according to the grammarians (ahl al-nahw).

The second view: the meaning of the verse is: "Indeed, I do not fear before Me the messengers, but others than the messengers fear; except for the one who wrongs, then substitutes good after evil, for he does not fear." The third view: the exception here is disjunctive (munqati'), and its meaning is: "But the one who wrongs, then fears; for whoever substitutes good after evil, he does not fear."

In some tafsirs it is stated that what is meant by His saying ﴿except for the one who wrongs﴾ is Musa, by his killing of the Copt; and as for his substituting good after evil, it is his repentance and remorse, and that is in the Exalted's saying: ﴿He said, "My Lord, I have wronged myself"﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 12:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And put your hand into your bosom; it will come out white without blemish﴾ — we have already explained it. In the narrative: it used to shine like lightning.

And His saying: ﴿among nine signs﴾ means: along with nine signs. It has also been said: from nine signs. Imru' al-Qays said:

[Wa-hal] yan'amanna man kana akhira 'ahdihi ... [thalathina] shahran fi thalathati ahwal

That is: from three states.

And His saying: ﴿to Pharaoh and his people; indeed, they were a people who were defiantly disobedient﴾ — that is: going out of obedience.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 27, verse 13:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿When Our signs came to them, clearly perceptible﴾, meaning: with clear evidence.

His saying: ﴿They said, "This is manifest sorcery."﴾ That is: evident sorcery.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 14:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they denied them﴾, meaning: they rejected them. The "bi" (ba') is extra (silah). It was also said: they denied by means of the evidence (dalala) that had appeared from them both.

And His saying: ﴿while their souls were convinced of them﴾, meaning: they had indeed known that they were from God, exalted is He.

And His saying: ﴿out of wrongdoing and arrogance﴾, meaning: polytheism (shirk) and haughtiness (takabbur).

And His saying: ﴿So see how was the end of the corrupters﴾, its meaning is apparent.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And We certainly gave David and Solomon knowledge﴾, meaning the knowledge of judgment (ʿilm al-qaḍāʾ, the science of legal judgment) and the knowledge of the speech of birds (manṭiq al-ṭayr) and the speech of animals (manṭiq al-dawābb). It is related from some of them that it was the knowledge of alchemy (ʿilm al-kīmiyāʾ), but this is a shādh (anomalous, weak or isolated) opinion.

His words: ﴿And they both said, "All praise is for Allah, who has favoured us over many of His believing servants."﴾ Its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 16:

The Most High said: ﴿And Solomon inherited from David﴾. The people of tafsir said: What is meant is not the inheritance of wealth; rather, what is meant is the inheritance of kingship and prophethood. David was a king and a prophet, [and likewise] Solomon was a king and a prophet. Solomon was given what David had been given of kingship, and he was additionally granted the subjugation of the wind, which had not been granted to his father; likewise the subjugation of the devils. Al-Kalbi said: David had nineteen male children, and Solomon inherited his kingship and prophethood from among them.

In some of the musnads, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that Allah the Most High commanded David to ask Solomon about ten questions: if he answered, he would be his successor. It is related that Allah the Most High sent to David a sealed scroll containing the answers to the questions. David gathered the rabbis and the monks, summoned Solomon, and asked him the questions. The ten questions were that David asked Solomon, may the blessings of Allah be upon them both: "What is the nearest of things? What is the farthest of things? What is the most intimate of things? What is the most lonely of things? What are the two things that stand? What are the two things that differ? What are the two things that hate each other? [What is that which, when used at the beginning of a matter, is praised at its end?] And what is that which, when used at the beginning of a matter, is blamed at its end?" He said: "As for the nearest of things, it is the Hereafter. As for the farthest of things, it is what has escaped you of the world. As for the most intimate of things, it is a body in which is its spirit. As for the most lonely of things, it is a body with no spirit in it. As for the two things that stand, they are the heavens and the earth. As for the two things that differ, they are the night and the day. As for the two things that hate each other, they are life and death. As for that which, when used at the beginning of a matter, is praised at its end, it is forbearance at the time of anger. As for that which, when used at the beginning of a matter, is blamed at its end, it is hastiness at the time of anger." When Solomon answered with these answers, the seal was removed from the scroll that Allah the Most High had sent, and behold, the answers were in accordance with what Solomon had said, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him.

In this report: when Solomon answered with these answers, the rabbis asked him another question: "What is the thing which, if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt?" He said: "It is the heart." The rabbis said to him: "You have the right to the caliphate, O Solomon." Then David, peace be upon him, appointed him as successor.

If it is said: If David appointed him as successor, how is the Most High's saying ﴿And Solomon inherited from David﴾ consistent? We say: The inheritance here means his standing in place of David in kingship, prophethood and knowledge; it does not mean the inheritance known in property. This is like their saying: "The scholars are the heirs of the prophets," and what is meant by it is what we have explained.

{We have been taught the speech of birds

And His saying: ﴿And he said: O people, we have been taught the speech of birds﴾. He called their voice "speech" because its meaning is understood, just as the meaning of human speech is understood, except that the voice of birds is of one form, while human voices are of various forms. It is possible that this was, in the time of Solomon specifically, a miracle for him, that he was given for their voices meanings that are understood, just as people understand one another.

Nafi' related, on the authority of Ibn Umar, that the Prophet said: "The white rooster is my friend, the friend of my friend, and the enemy of my enemy." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, and what does it say?" He said: "It says: Remember Allah, you heedless ones." This report is gharib.

In some of the musnads: a group of Jews came to Abdullah ibn Abbas and said to him: "We are going to ask you about things; if you answer us, we will embrace Islam." He said: "Ask for understanding, and do not ask to trip up." They said: "What does the priest say in his whistling? The rooster in his crowing? The frog in his croaking? The donkey in his braying? The horse in his neighing? And what does the starling or the partridge say?" He said: "As for the priest, he says: O Allah, curse the haters of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. As for the rooster, he says: Remember Allah, you heedless ones. As for the frog, he says: Glory be to the Worshipped One in the depths of the seas. As for the donkey, he says: O Allah, curse the tax collectors. As for the horse, when it whinnies at the meeting of the two lines, it says: Most Holy, Most Pure, Lord of the angels and the Spirit. As for the starling, it says: O Allah, I ask You for the sustenance of each day, O Provider. As for the partridge, it says: The Most Merciful is established upon the Throne." He said: So the Jews embraced Islam.

It has been established from the Prophet that he said concerning the donkey: "When it brays, it has seen a devil."

His saying ﴿and we have been given of everything﴾ means: of everything that is given to prophets and kings. It was also said that he said this in the manner of abundance and exaggeration, like the saying of one who says: "I spoke to everyone about your need."

His saying ﴿Indeed, this is truly the manifest bounty﴾ means: the clear excess over all creation.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 17:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And there were gathered for Solomon his hosts﴾. Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: His encampment was a hundred farsakh (a unit of distance, roughly three miles): twenty-five farsakh for mankind, twenty-five farsakh for the jinn, twenty-five farsakh for the wild beasts, and twenty-five farsakh for the birds.

And on the authority of Sa'id ibn Jubayr: Six hundred thousand chairs would be set out for Solomon; mankind would sit nearest to him, then the jinn would sit beyond them, then the birds would shade them, and then the wind would carry them. He, may Allah be pleased with him, said: Abu 'Ali al-Shafi'i informed us, Abu al-Hasan ibn Faras informed us, al-Dibali informed us, Sa'id ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Makhzumi informed us, Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna informed us, on the authority of Ibn Salam, on the authority of Sa'id ibn Jubayr ... the report.

And His words: ﴿So they were being marshalled﴾, meaning: they were being driven on. It was also said: they were being gathered. The well-known opinion is: they were being restrained, and its meaning is: the first of them is held back until the last of them catches up. The poet said:

(When I rebuked white hair for youth, saying: "Enough, you have grown sound, and white hair is a restrainer.")

And on the authority of al-Hasan al-Basri, he said: People must have restrainers (wizah, guards). He said this when he took up the judgeship and people crowded around him.

And on the authority of 'Uthman, he said: What the ruler restrains is more than what the Qur'an restrains. Its meaning: what people refrain from out of fear of the ruler is more than what people refrain from out of fear of the Qur'an.

﴿Until, when they came upon the valley of the ants, an ant said: "O ants, enter your dwellings..."﴾

And on the authority of some scholars regarding the difference between 'Umar and 'Uthman: 'Umar had a bad opinion of people, so he was strict in the matter and his subjects were made righteous; 'Uthman had a good opinion of people, so he was lenient in the matter and his subjects became corrupt.

In the story: Solomon, upon him be blessings from Allah, had over every class of mankind, jinn, birds and beasts a restrainer (wizah).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 18:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Until, when they came upon the valley of the ants﴾. It is said: it is a valley in Syria (al-Sham). Ka'b said: it is a valley in al-Ta'if. Some of them said: it was a valley whose inhabitants were jinn, and those ants were their mounts, and they were like wolves. It was also said: they were like Bakhti camels (a two-humped breed). The well-known view is that they were small ants, and they were named "naml" (ants) because of their tanmul, that is, because of the abundance of their movement.

It is related from 'Adi ibn Hatim that he used to crumble bread for the ants. He (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Abu 'Ali al-Shafi'i informed us of this with that chain of narration, and what we have narrated from Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna, from Mas'ud, from a man, from 'Adi ibn Hatim.

His words: ﴿A certain ant said﴾. It is possible that Allah, may He be exalted, created for the ants at that time a comprehensible speech. In the Arabic usage, ants belong to the category of al-hakl, and al-hakl is that which has no voice. The poet said:

(He taught Sulayman the hakl)

His words: ﴿O you ants, enter your dwellings﴾. He did not say "idkhulي" (feminine address), though the correct grammatical form would be "idkhuli" (feminine). Rather, "idkhulu" (masculine plural) is used for the children of Adam, but since they spoke in a manner like the speech of the sons of Adam, they were addressed as the sons of Adam are addressed.

His words: ﴿Lest Sulayman and his hosts crush you﴾, that is: lest the crushing of destruction overwhelm you. (It was also said: lest they trample you.) If someone asks: how is this consistent, since it was the wind that carried Sulayman? It is related that Sulayman and his hosts used to gather on a carpet, and the wind carried the carpet. The answer: it is possible that among them were those who walked, and the earth was folded up for them; and it is possible that this was before the wind was subjected to Sulayman, and Allah knows best. If it is said: ants were not among the birds, yet he had been taught the speech of the birds? The answer to this: al-Sha'bi said: they were ants that had wings, so they would be birds.

His words: ﴿while they do not perceive﴾. The people of tafsir said: the ants knew that Sulayman was a king who had no tyranny or oppression. The meaning of the verse: if you do not enter your dwellings, he would trample you without noticing you, and had they known, they would not have trampled. In the narrative too: when Sulayman reached the valley of the ants, he halted his troops until the ants had entered their dwellings. Also in the narrative: Sulayman heard the speech of the ants from three miles away, and Allah had commanded the wind to bring him every news and every speech. In the verse there is evidence that killing ants is disliked. It is related from al-Hasan al-Basri that he said regarding the verse ﴿Indeed, the righteous are in bliss﴾: they are those who do not harm the dharr, which is small ants. If it is asked: how is it valid to attribute such knowledge to ants? The answer: it is permissible that Allah creates in them this kind of understanding and knowledge, and it is said that they are swift in their perception. When an ant takes a grain of wheat, it cuts it into two halves so that it does not sprout; and when it takes coriander seed, it cuts it into four pieces, because coriander seed, if cut into two pieces, will sprout, but if cut into four pieces, it will not sprout.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 19:

The Exalted's words: ﴿So he smiled, laughing at her speech﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: The laughter of the prophets is smiling.

And His words: ﴿laughing﴾ mean: smiling. It is said: at first it was smiling, and at its end it was laughter. If it is asked: why did he laugh? The answer is in two respects. The first: joy at the ant's praise of him. The second: he heard something wondrous, and whoever hears something wondrous laughs, and it may overcome him in that.

And His words: ﴿And he said, "My Lord, enable me﴾ mean: inspire me.

And His words: ﴿to be grateful for Your favour which You have bestowed upon me﴾. It is said: gratitude is the opening of the heart to seeing the bounty. It is also said: it is praise of Allah the Exalted for His blessing.

His words: ﴿and upon my parents﴾ mean: his father Dawud and his mother Aysa.

And His words: ﴿and to do righteousness that You will approve﴾ mean: of Your obedience.

And His words: ﴿and admit me by Your mercy among Your righteous servants﴾ mean: with Your righteous servants into Paradise.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 20:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And he inspected the birds﴾. Tafaqqud is seeking what has been lost.

And His saying: ﴿Why is it that I do not see the hoopoe?﴾ The hoopoe (hudhhud) is a well-known bird. If it is asked: why did he seek it? The answer has two aspects. The first: the birds used to shade Sulayman and his army from the sun, so he looked and saw the place of the hoopoe empty, with the sun striking the spot where it had been, so he sought it for this reason. The second: what is related from Ibn 'Abbas, that the hoopoe used to know the location of water in the earth, and it would see water beneath the ground as one sees it in a glass, and it would state how near or far the water was. Sulayman needed water on his journey, so he sought the hoopoe for that purpose. It is related that Nafi' ibn al-Azraq was with Ibn 'Abbas while he was mentioning this, and he said: "O Wassaf, look at what you are saying, for a boy among us sets a snare and covers it with dust, and the hoopoe comes and falls into the snare." Ibn 'Abbas said to him: "Indeed, destiny (al-qadar) comes between sight and vision." It is also related that he said: "When the decree (al-qada') and destiny (al-qadar) come, the intellect and the sight depart."

And His saying: ﴿Or is he among the absent?﴾ That is: "Is he among the absent?" The mim in it is a filler (silah), as if he turned away from the first statement and mentioned this in the form of a question. It is said that when he said: ﴿Why is it that I do not see the hoopoe?﴾ doubt entered him, so he said: "Is he present or absent?"

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 21:

The Exalted's saying: ﴿I will surely punish him with a severe punishment﴾. Concerning this there are several opinions. The first, and it is the most well-known, is that he plucks out his feathers and throws him into the sun, so the ants eat him. It is also said: it is his imprisonment together with his opposite. It is also said: it is his removal from his own kind to another kind, and that is the severe punishment.

And His saying: ﴿or I will slaughter him﴾ is clear in meaning.

And His saying: ﴿or he must bring me a clear authority﴾, that is: a manifest excuse. It is also said: a clear proof. In the narrative: the commander of the birds was the kurkur (a kind of bird), so Sulayman asked him in the presence of the hoopoe whether he was present or absent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 22:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then he tarried not long﴾, meaning: not for a long time.

And His saying: ﴿Then he said, "I have comprehended that which you have not comprehended"﴾. There is an ellipsis (hadhf) in it, and its meaning is: the hoopoe came and Sulayman, peace be upon him, asked him about his absence, and he said: ﴿I have comprehended that which you have not comprehended﴾.

In the story: when the hoopoe was informed of Sulayman's statement, ﴿"I will surely punish him with severe punishment or slaughter him"﴾, the hoopoe said: "Did the Prophet of God make an exception?" They said: "Yes, he said: (or he shall bring me a clear authority)." He said: "Then I am saved."

If someone says: punishment only occurs after one is legally responsible (taklif), and the hoopoe was not legally responsible; and if he was not legally responsible, he was not disobedient by absenting himself, and if he was not disobedient, he does not deserve punishment? The answer to this: it is possible that God, may He be exalted, gave the birds at that time the capacity by which they understood the command, so their prohibition from absence and from neglecting the station of service was valid, and so when they were negligent, they deserved punishment.

As for His saying: ﴿I have comprehended that which you have not comprehended﴾, ihata (comprehension) is knowledge of a thing from all its aspects.

And His saying: ﴿And I have come to you from Saba'﴾. It was also read as "Saba'" without tanwin. Whoever applies tanwin to Saba' treats it as the name of a man. In some tafsirs it is reported from the Prophet that he was asked about Saba' and said: "He was a man who had ten sons; six of them turned right (tayammun) and four of them turned left (tashā'um). As for those who turned right, they are Kindah, al-Ash'ar, al-Azd, Himyar, Madhhij, and Anmar. As for those who turned left, they are Lakhm, Judham, 'Amilah, and Ghassan."

Whoever does not apply tanwin makes it the name of a place. Know that the Arabs sometimes applied tanwin to Saba' and sometimes did not. The poet said, applying tanwin to Saba':

(Those who came down, and Taym, on the heights of Saba' ... the hides of buffaloes have bitten their necks)

And another said, not applying tanwin:

(Of Saba', the residents of Ma'rib, when ... they build beyond its torrent the great dam)

And His saying: ﴿with certain news﴾, meaning: with true information.

"Indeed, I found a woman ruling over them" (﴿إِنِّي وجدت امْرَأَة تملكهم﴾). This woman is Bilqis, daughter of Sharahil. Mujahid said: "She had forty kings as her ancestors, the last of whom was her father." And it is reported from Qatadah that he said: "One of her parents was from the jinn." And it is reported from al-Hasan al-Basri that he said: "They entrusted their affairs to a woman whose breasts were shaking [i.e., a woman of little consequence]."

It is firmly established, by the transmission of Abu Bakrah, when news reached him that the non-Arabs (al-'Ajam) had appointed over them the daughter of Kisra, [the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "A people who entrust their affairs to a woman will never prosper."]

And it is reported from Khalid ibn Safwan in dispraise of Yemen: "They are among those who tan hides, who tend monkeys, and who weave cloaks. A woman ruled over them, a hoopoe guided them, and a mouse drowned them."

Know that the people of Yemen are praised by the tongue of the Prophet (ﷺ), and the dispraise we have mentioned applies only to the polytheists among them.

As for His saying, ﴿وَأُوتِيت من كل شَيْء﴾ ("and she has been given of everything"), it means: of everything that such a queen is given.

As for His saying, ﴿وَلها عرش عَظِيم﴾ ("and she has a mighty throne"), it means: a great, massive seat. In the narration, the length of the throne was eighty cubits by eighty in width. It was also said to be less than that, and Allah knows best.

They said: it was adorned with jewels, rubies, and chrysolite, and the like of that.

And His saying: ﴿I found her and her people prostrating to the sun instead of Allah, and Satan has made their deeds appealing to them and barred them from the path﴾, that is, from the path of Islam.

And His saying: ﴿so they are not guided﴾, that is, to the right way.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 25:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So that they do not prostrate to Allah﴾. It was also read as "alla yasjudu" with the letter (lam) lightened (alā yasjudū, with light alif-lam). As for the one who read ﴿illā﴾ with the letter (lam) doubled (shaddah), its meaning is: "He barred them from the way, so that they would not prostrate" — that is, "lest they prostrate" (li-alla yasjudū). It was also said that its meaning is: "Satan made their deeds appear fair to them, so that they would not prostrate." On this reading there is no prostration upon reciting it, as the people of tafsir have mentioned. As for the reading with the lightened letter, the meaning of his saying "alā yasjudū" is: "Ala, O people, prostrate!" (alā yā hā'ulā'i usjudū).

(Alā yasalmā yā dārāmī ʿalā al-balā... wa lā zāla mamhalan bi-jurʿāʾika al-qaṭr)

Its meaning is: "Alā yā aslamī yā dār" (Ala, O abode, be safe). Another said:

(Alā yasalmā yā Hind Hind banī ... Badr wa in kāna ḥayyānā ghadā ākhira al-dahr)

Its meaning is: "Alā yā aslamī Hind" (Ala, O Hind, be safe). It is possible that this is from the speech of the hoopoe (hudhhud), and it is possible that it is from the speech of Allah, exalted is He, from the outset. The people of tafsir said: On this reading, prostration is recommended (yusann al-sajdah), because it is a command to prostrate. Some of them said: On the first reading, one also prostrates, in opposition to the polytheists.

As for His saying: ﴿Allah, who brings forth what is hidden (al-khabʾ) in the heavens and the earth﴾, that is, whatever is hidden in the heavens and the earth. What is hidden in the sky is the rain, and what is hidden in the earth is the plants. It was also said: [everything] that is hidden.

As for His saying: ﴿And He knows what you conceal and what you disclose﴾, its meaning is apparent.

Allah's words: ﴿Allah—there is no deity except Him, the Lord of the Great Throne﴾. The Throne is mentioned here because He had told of her having a great throne, and the purpose of the mention is that her throne was small and insignificant in comparison with the Throne of Allah, exalted is He.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿He said, "We will see whether you have told the truth or were among the liars."﴾ In this is evidence that kings must verify what they are told.

And His saying, ﴿or were among the liars﴾: meaning, "or are you among the liars?" Here أم (am) is used with the sense of "rather" or "or," and the question is one of confirmation.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 28:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Go with this letter of mine and throw it to them, then turn away from them﴾. They said: In it there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir), and its meaning is: throw it to them, then watch what they return, then turn away from them. It was also said that its meaning is: turn away from them, i.e., withdraw from them, then watch what they return. Some of them said: The hoopoe (al-hudhud) taught the etiquette of entering upon kings, meaning: when the one entering comes upon a king, he should not linger, but rather leave immediately, then return and seek the answer.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 29:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿She said: O chiefs (al-mala')﴾. In the verse there is an ellipsis (hadhf), namely that the hoopoe (al-hudhud) went and carried the letter. In the narrative: he entered upon her through the window (kuwwa), while she was in seclusion (khalwa), reclining on her couch, and he dropped the letter on her chest. It is also said: she was sleeping, so he placed it beside her. And it is said: he took the letter away and dropped it on her lap, in the presence of a gathering of people. As for al-mala', they are the nobles (ashraf) and elders (kubara') of the people. And it is said: she had three hundred and thirteen commanders (qa'id), each commander over twelve thousand [men]. And it is said: she had twelve thousand commanders, each commander over a thousand men.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, a noble letter has been delivered to me﴾, that is: fine (hasan). And it is said: sealed (makhtum). In the reports from the Prophet (ﷺ), by way of Ibn 'Abbas: "Part of the nobility of a letter is its sealing." The third opinion: a noble letter, that is, its writer and sender are noble.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 30:

The words of the Most High, ﴿Indeed, it is from Sulayman﴾: in the exegesis it is said that Sulayman had written: "From the servant of Allah, Sulayman son of Dawud, to Bilqis daughter of Sharahil: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Do not exalt yourselves over me, and come to me in submission (muslimin)."

The scholars said: this letter is the most concise of letters, for it combined the address, the letter and the purpose within two lines, and the letters of the prophets were of the utmost brevity.

It is related from al-Sha'bi (Amir ibn Sharahil al-Sha'bi): "The Messenger [of Allah] used to write at first, 'In Your name, O Allah' (bismika Allahumma). When Allah the Most High revealed His words, ﴿In the name of Allah be its course and its anchorage﴾, he wrote, 'In the name of Allah.' When Allah the Most High revealed, ﴿Say: Call upon Allah or call upon the Most Merciful﴾, he wrote, 'In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful.' When Allah the Most High revealed in Surat al-Naml, ﴿Indeed, it is from Sulayman, and indeed it is: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate﴾, he wrote, 'In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.'"

ʿAsim said: I said to al-Sha'bi, "I saw a letter of the Prophet beginning with 'In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful.'" He said: "That is the third letter."

It is related from Buraydah (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "I know a verse that was revealed to me which was not revealed to any prophet after Sulayman son of Dawud. By Allah, I will not leave the mosque until I inform you of it." He said: So he stood and put one of his feet out of the mosque. I said to myself: he has sworn. Then he turned to me and said to me: "With what do you open your prayer?" meaning your recitation. I said: "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate." He said: "It is it," then he went out.

Almighty God says: ﴿Do not exalt yourselves against me﴾. That is, do not magnify yourselves against me. It is also said: do not be arrogant toward me. Its meaning is: do not refuse and abandon responding (to me), for refusal and abandoning the response stem from haughtiness and arrogance.

And His saying: ﴿and come to me in submission﴾ has two interpretations. One of them: it is from Islam (submission to God in faith). The other: it is from istislam (surrender and submission).

"She said, 'O eminent ones, advise me concerning my affair.'" She said this by way of consultation, because she knew that Sulayman's kingdom was greater than her kingdom. And His saying, "Advise me concerning my affair" means: answer me concerning my affair.

And His saying, "I am not one to decide a matter" means: not one who issues a judgment or finalizes a matter, "until you are present" means: until you attend.

Ibn Mas'ud recited: "I was not a judge of a matter" (مَا كنت قاضية أمرا).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 33:

The words of the Most High: ﴿They said, "We are possessors of strength and possessors of great might"﴾ — they informed (her) of their large numbers and their courage.

And His words: ﴿And the command is yours﴾ — then they returned the command to her, that she might fight or refrain from fighting. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿So see what you will command﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 34:

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, when kings enter a town, they ruin it﴾, meaning: they devastate it.

And His saying: ﴿and they make the honoured people of it humiliated﴾. The "honoured" (a'izzah, plural of 'aziz) are the people who refuse to accept humiliation through their strength and power. Making them "humiliated" in this place is only by enslavement and subjugation.

And His saying: ﴿and thus do they do﴾. Most of the exegetes hold that this is from the speech of Allah, Exalted is He, by way of affirming her statement, not by way of quoting her.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 35:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And I am going to send them a gift﴾. The hadiyya (gift) is a giving in the manner of reciprocation, and gifts between brothers are recommended. It has been narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Exchange gifts, and you will love one another."

It is also established from the Prophet (ﷺ) that "he would accept gifts and would reject charity."

And it has been narrated from him that he said: "The gifts of rulers are embezzlement (ghulul)."

It is narrated that a man gave 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) a gift of a slaughtered camel's leg, and there was a dispute between him and another man. When the two of them came before him, he said: "O Commander of the Faithful, judge between me and him as the leg is separated from the camel." He said: "You are that man." Then he returned the camel's leg to him and ruled against him.

As for His words: ﴿So the envoys will return with what?﴾, it is narrated that she said: "If he is a king, I will satisfy him with wealth; but if he is a prophet, he will not be satisfied with wealth."

As for the gift she sent to Sulayman, it is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: it was a hundred male servants and a hundred female servants.

And from Mujahid that he said: two hundred boys and two hundred girls.

Some of them resembled one another in appearance, voice and bearing, and she said to the messenger: "Tell him: let him distinguish between the boys [and the girls]."

And from Sa'id ibn Jubayr that he said: she sent him a golden brick wrapped in brocade. It is also narrated that she sent him a great many items of silk, camphor, musk and perfume.

In the story: she sent him two beads, one of which had no hole, and the other had a crooked hole, and she asked him to thread the string through the crooked hole without the treatment of man or jinn, and to pierce the other bead without the treatment of man or jinn. She also sent him a cup, and asked him to fill it with water that had neither descended from the sky nor sprung from the earth.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 36:

The words of the Most High: ﴿When he came to Sulayman, he said: "Would you provide me with wealth?"﴾ The imdad (reinforcement, supplying) is attaching the second things to the first. It was also said: it is that the second is attached to the first, the third to the second, and the fourth to the third, and so on until it ends.

And His words: ﴿What Allah has given me is better than what He has given you﴾ means: what Allah has given me of prophethood, kingship and wealth is better than what He has given you.

And His words: ﴿Rather, you rejoice in your gift﴾ mean: some of you rejoice in giving gifts to one another, but as for me, I do not rejoice in your gifts.

In the narrative: the woman had said to the envoys: "If Sulayman is a king, he will not seat you, but if he is a prophet, he will seat you." It is narrated that when the messengers came and drew near to Sulayman, Jibril (peace be upon him) came and informed him of their arrival and what they had with them. Sulayman then commanded that bricks (libanat) of gold and silver be placed, until they were put beneath the feet of the animals, and the animals began to defecate and urinate upon them. When the envoys saw that, they belittled what they had.

Also in the narrative: when they entered, they stood, and Sulayman (peace be upon him) said to them: "Allah, the Most High, has raised the sky and spread the earth, so whoever wishes may sit and whoever wishes may stand."

It is narrated that he commanded them to sit, and he summoned the boys and girls to perform wudu. Whoever poured the water on the inner part of the forearm, he said: "She is a girl," and whoever poured the water on the back of the forearm, he said: "He is a boy."

It is also narrated that he made whoever began the washing with the elbow a boy, and whoever began the washing with the wrist a girl. It is narrated that he made whoever scooped the water from the vessel a boy, and whoever poured water over his hand a girl.

He summoned the two pearls, and a worm that lives in the green plant came, and it was said: in the willow. It said: "I will thread the string through this hole, on condition that my provision be in the willow." So that was granted to it, and the string was tied to it. It was also said: it took the string in its mouth and entered the hole, and came out from the other side. As for the other pearl, a worm came that lives in fruits, and it pierced the pearl on condition that its provision be in fruits, so that was granted to it. Then he summoned the bowl and commanded that the horses be made to run, and he filled the bowl with their sweat. Then he returned the gifts to the envoys, until they returned them to the woman.

The scholars said: The prophets did not accept the gifts of the polytheists.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 37:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Return to them, for we shall surely come to them with hosts that they cannot withstand﴾. That is: they have no power to withstand them.

And His words: ﴿and we shall surely drive them out from it, abased﴾. That is: from their lands. And His words: ﴿and they will be humbled﴾. That is: we shall drive them out in a state of humiliation and degradation, and this takes the form of being taken captive and enslaved, and what is similar to that.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 38:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He said, "O chiefs, which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?"﴾ Most of the exegetes hold that Sulayman said this after the messenger had returned and the gifts had been rejected. If someone says: when he rejected the gifts, how did he then ask for her throne and her seat? The answer to this is given in several ways.

The first: he wished that this throne should be his, and it had been described to him.

The second: he wished to see it, for it had been said to him that it was made of gold, its legs were of jewels, and it was adorned with pearls.

The third: he intended to show her a great miracle, for it is related that she had placed that throne within seven chambers, one inside the other, had locked the doors and secured them. So he wished to show her her throne in his presence, so that when she saw this great miracle she would believe.

As for His saying, ﴿Which of you will bring me her throne﴾, we have already explained it. As for His saying, ﴿before they come to me in submission﴾, that is, submitting. It was also said that it is from Islam (submission). In the narrative: Bilqis set out with her armies toward Sulayman, peace be upon him, seeking reconciliation and entering into his obedience.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 39:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿A ifrit from the jinn said﴾. It was recited in the irregular reading (shadh): "A ifriyah from the jinn said." The ifrit (ʿifrīt, a mighty and powerful one) is the strong, powerful one. In some tafsir works it is said that he was Sakhr the jinn, and it is narrated that he was like a mountain, and he would place his foot at the furthest point of his gaze.

His saying: ﴿I will bring it to you before you rise from your place﴾, meaning: before you rise from your seat. ﴿The one who had knowledge of the Scripture said: I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you﴾, referring to the seat where he sat to judge between the people. His sitting extended from the morning until near midday. In the narration: the woman had reached about a farsakh (a league). When Sulayman heard that, he said, seeking the throne...

His saying: ﴿And indeed I am strong and trustworthy over it﴾, strong for carrying the throne, trustworthy regarding what is upon it of jewels.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 40:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Said one who had knowledge from the Scripture﴾. It is related that when this ifrit said thus, Sulayman said: "I want it faster than that." Then the one who had knowledge from the Scripture said: ﴿I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you.﴾

Scholars differed concerning the one who had knowledge from the Scripture. The most well-known opinions are that he was Asif ibn Barkhiya ibn Simi'a, a righteous man among the Children of Israel, who knew the Greatest Name of Allah (al-ism al-a'zam, the Greatest Name).

The second opinion is that he was al-Khidr, mentioned by Ibn Lahi'a. The third opinion is that he was an angel from among the angels, cited by Ibn Bakhr. The fourth opinion is that he was Sulayman (peace be upon him), and this is a well-known view, but the soundest is the first opinion.

Scholars also differed over what he invoked Allah with. Some of them said that he said: "O my God and God of all creation, one God, there is no god but You, bring it." It is related that he said: "O Living, O Self-Subsisting (Qayyum)." It is also related that he said: "O Possessor of Majesty and Honour." And Allah knows best.

His saying: ﴿before your glance returns to you﴾ has several interpretations. One is that he raised his gaze to the sky, and before he returned it to the earth, he saw the Throne (al-'arsh) beside him. Some said it means that he blinks once. Some said it means that he looks at a man coming, and before that man reaches him, the Throne has reached him. Some said it means that he looks at a man departing, and before his glance returns from that departing man, the Throne has reached him.

In the narrative: when he invoked Allah, Allah split the earth beneath its base, and the Throne sank into the earth and appeared beside the throne of Sulayman, and the distance was that of two months. Some said that Allah annihilated that throne and brought into existence a likeness of it in its form beside Sulayman. The first opinion is the more preferable.

His saying: ﴿So when he saw it settled beside him﴾. Al-Suddi said: Sulayman was dismayed when he saw this, and his dismay was that how could that man do what he himself was unable to do? Then he returned to himself and said: ﴿This is of the bounty of my Lord, to test me whether I will be grateful or ungrateful.﴾

His saying: ﴿And whoever is grateful, he is grateful only for [the benefit of] himself; and whoever is ungrateful - indeed, my Lord is Free of need and Generous.﴾ That is: free of need of his gratitude, and generous in accepting his gratitude and rewarding him for it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 41:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Disguise her throne for her﴾ mean: change her throne for her. And His words: ﴿We shall see whether she is guided or is among those who are not guided﴾ — in the tafsir: the jinn had said to Sulayman, peace be upon him: "Indeed, there is something in her intellect." They also said to him: "Indeed, her shin is like the hoof of a donkey, and on her leg there is much hair." He only altered her throne so that her intellect might be known by this. It is narrated that he made its top its bottom and its bottom its top. It is narrated that he replaced the red jewels with green, and the green with red. It is narrated that he added to it and subtracted from it.

And His words, may He be exalted: ﴿We shall see whether she is guided or is among those who are not guided﴾ mean: will she recognize her throne or will she not recognize it?

The commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on Surah 27, verse 42:

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So when she arrived, it was said, "Is your throne like this?" She said, "It is as if it were it."﴾ She did not say "No," fearing to lie, nor did she say "Yes," fearing to lie; rather, she said, "It is as if it were it." Muqatil said: "They confused her, so she confused them, though she had known it." It is related that it was only confused for her because she had left the throne behind in her houses, and she saw it in front of her at Sulayman's, so the matter became confused for her, and she said what she said.

As for His saying: ﴿And we were given knowledge before her﴾, this is from the speech of Sulayman, meaning: we knew her state, her affair, and the state of her throne before she knew. As for His saying: ﴿and we were Muslims﴾, meaning: submitting to Allah, obedient to Him.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 43:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And what she used to worship besides Allah had kept her away﴾ (meaning: what she used to worship besides Allah kept her away from worshipping Allah).

And His words: ﴿Indeed, she was from a disbelieving people﴾ are clear in meaning.

She was an Arab woman, one of the kings of Yemen. Some of them said: His words, "that she was from a disbelieving people," he said this because she was from a people of Magians who worship the sun. And from some of them: he said the meaning of His words, ﴿And what she used to worship besides Allah had kept her away﴾ is: what kept her away from worshipping Allah was the deficiency of her intellect, rather, [it was] what she used to worship besides Allah, because the jinn had said to Solomon: indeed, there is in her intellect [something].

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 27, verse 44:

The words of God Most High: ﴿It was said to her: "Enter the palace (al-sarh)."﴾ Al-sarh, in its original linguistic sense, is an elevated place. Abu 'Ubayd mentioned this in Gharib al-Musannaf and elsewhere.

As for al-sarh here, there are several opinions. Mujahid said: it is a pool of water covered with glass (qawarir).

Al-Zajjaj said: al-sarh, al-sarha, al-saha and al-baha have one meaning, which is the courtyard (al-sahn). It is also reported from some of them that al-sarh is the palace (al-qasr), and it was said that it is the house (al-bayt).

In the narrative: the jinn said to Sulayman, "Her hind leg is like the hoof of a donkey, and she is hairy-legged." They feared that Sulayman would marry her and she would inform him of the secrets of the jinn, and her mother was a jinniyya. So Sulayman, peace be upon him, wished to see her leg, and he ordered the construction of a great pool, in which he placed a large number of fish, frogs and similar creatures. Then he ordered that the water be covered with a sheet of glass. In some reports, he made a courtyard of glass and placed beneath it figures of fish and frogs, so that whoever saw it thought it was water. It is also related that Sulayman, peace be upon him, ordered his throne to be placed in the middle of the palace, then invited her to his assembly. When she reached the palace and looked, she thought it was water, so she uncovered her shins to enter the water. Sulayman cried out: ﴿Indeed, it is a palace paved smooth with glass﴾, and he saw her shins, and there was much hair on them.

Some of them mentioned that he saw a delicate foot and a fine shin, and that there was hair on it.

If someone says: why did Sulayman seek this sight? The answer to this has two aspects. The first: he wished to know whether the jinn were truthful or lying. The second: he wished to marry her, so he intended to look at her shins, since they had said that there was hair on them.

The people of tafsir have mentioned that Sulayman, peace be upon him, asked the devils: "What removes hair?" So they made depilatory cream (al-nura), and he was the first to make use of the bathhouse (al-hamam) and depilatory cream.

[And His words: ﴿So when she saw it, she thought it was a deep water and uncovered her shins. He said: "Indeed, it is a palace paved smooth with glass."﴾]

Mumarrad means smooth (mumallas). It was also said that mumarrad means wide in length and breadth. The poet said:

(I went out early in the morning and found them, before forenoon, and the Babylonian smooth one...)

As for His words: ﴿"My Lord, I have wronged myself"﴾, that is, by shirk. It is said that when she reached the palace and thought it was a deep pool of water, she said to herself: "Sulayman wants to drown me," and fighting would have been easier than this.

His words: ﴿I have wronged myself﴾ mean, by that assumption.

His words: ﴿And I have submitted with Sulayman to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ are clear in meaning. Whoever submits with a prophet is, by that, with that prophet in submission to Allah. Some of them have mentioned that he married her. It is related that 'Abd Allah ibn 'Utba was asked about this, and he said: "It ends at His words: ﴿And I have submitted with Sulayman to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾," meaning that there is no knowledge beyond that.

As for the duration of Sulayman's reign, they differed about it. It is related that the kingship came to him when he was thirteen years old, and he died when he was fifty-three. In some reports from Abu Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali, it is said that he ruled for seven hundred years, but this is a strange report.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 45:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We certainly sent to Thamud their brother Salih, [saying], "Worship Allah"﴾ meaning: affirm the oneness of Allah.

And His saying: ﴿and suddenly they were two factions disputing﴾ meaning: a believer and a disbeliever. And from Qatadah: one who affirms and one who denies.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 46:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Why do you seek to hasten the evil before the good?﴾ That is: why do you seek to hasten the punishment before the mercy? They had said to Salih: "If you are truthful, then bring us the punishment."

And His words: ﴿Why do you not seek forgiveness from Allah?﴾ That is: why do you not seek forgiveness from Allah? And istighfar (seeking forgiveness) here carries the meaning of tawbah (repentance).

His words: ﴿So that you may receive mercy﴾ — its meaning is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 47:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿They said, "We consider you and those with you to be a bad omen."﴾ That is: we take you and those with you as an ill omen (tatayyur, taking omens from things seen or heard). There are two views regarding the reason for their saying this. The first is that they said it because their community had been divided. The second view is that they said it because drought and famine befell them, so they said to Salih: "This is because of your ill omen."

Know that tiyarah (ominous augury, taking bad omens) is forbidden. In some reports from the Prophet (ﷺ): "There is no contagion (adwa) and no tiyarah."

And from him (ﷺ): "He used to love fa'l (good omen) and dislike tiyarah."

In some of the musnad collections, from the Prophet (ﷺ), he said: "The son of Adam will not be free from three things: from suspicion (zann), envy (hasad), and tiyarah. So when you suspect, do not be certain; when you envy, do not act upon it; and when you take a bad omen, proceed anyway."

In some reports: "No one is free from tiyarah, and tawakkul (trust) in Allah removes it."

The people of the Jahiliyyah used to take omens. A man among them, when he went out for some need and a bird flew by, or he met something, or heard a word, would take it as an omen, either to refrain from that action or to proceed with it. Some poets said:

"By your life, the diviners do not know by pebbles, nor do the bird-callers know what Allah is doing."

And al-Khalil ibn Ahmad said concerning the stars:

"Convey on my behalf to the astrologer that I am a disbeliever in what the stars have decreed.
Knowing that what will be and what has been is a decree from the Almighty, and it is obligatory."

His saying: ﴿He said, "Your omen is with Allah."﴾ That is: what befalls you of good and evil is from Allah. It is called a "bird" (ṭā'ir) because of the speed of its descent upon a person, for nothing descends more swiftly than a binding decree. It is also said: ﴿Your omen is with Allah﴾ means your deeds are with Allah, and it was called a "bird" because of the swiftness of its ascent to the heaven.

His saying: ﴿Rather, you are a people being tested.﴾ That is: you are being tried and examined. It is also said: you are being punished.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 48:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And in the city there were nine men (rahṭ) who made mischief in the land and did not reform.﴾ These nine are the ones who agreed upon hamstringing the she-camel, and their leader in that was Qudar ibn Salif, who was the one who undertook to hamstring her.

And His words: ﴿who made mischief in the land and did not reform﴾. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: by clipping (kasr) the dirhams and the dinars. And it is related from Qatadah: by tracking down the faults (awrat) of the people. And it was said: by sins and the commission of evil deeds (al-manakir).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 49:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They said: "Swear to one another by Allah"﴾ meaning: swear by Allah.

And His saying: ﴿"that we will surely attack him"﴾ meaning: that we will kill him by night, by bayat (by night attack). They said this to Salih.

And His saying: ﴿"and his family"﴾ meaning: and his people who had believed along with him.

And His saying: ﴿"Then we will surely say to his heir: 'We did not witness the destruction of his family'"﴾. It is also recited as "mahlak" with a fatha on the mim (mahlaka). It is permissible that it means the act of destroying (al-ihlak), and it is permissible that what is meant by it is the place of destruction (mawdi' al-halak).

And His saying: ﴿"and indeed we are truthful"﴾ meaning: we deny the killing of Salih. They said this because they feared his tribe (ʿashira).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 50:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And they plotted a plot, and We plotted a plot, while they did not perceive﴾. That is: they devised a scheme, and We devised a scheme. It is related that Allah, may He be exalted, sent the angels upon them until they crushed their heads with stones. Al-Dahhak said: Salih used to enter a cave in the mountain to worship Allah, so they schemed to enter upon him and kill him by stealth. They set off and began to lie in wait for that, but a stone fell down from the top of the mountain, so they fled and entered [the cave], and the rock fell upon the mouth of the cave and sealed them in. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿and We plotted a plot﴾.

And His words: ﴿while they did not perceive﴾ mean: they did not know how We had plotted against them.

Almost-complete translation below.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So look at how the outcome of their scheming turned out﴾. That is: what their scheming came to.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed We destroyed them and their people, all of them﴾. That is: We destroyed them and their people, all of them.

God's words, "So those are their houses, desolate because they wronged," meaning: desolate because they disbelieved.

And His words, "Indeed in that is a sign for a people who know," meaning: who know Our arrangement and Our scheming against the disbelievers.

Translation:

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We saved those who believed and used to be mindful of God﴾ — this has already been explained. And in the narrative: when God, exalted is He, destroyed the people of Salih, Salih came to Mecca and died there, and likewise Hud, peace be upon him.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 54:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And [mention] Lot, when he said to his people: "Do you commit an abomination while you see [it]?"﴾ That is: while you know that it is an abomination. It was also said that the meaning of His words ﴿while you see [it]﴾ is: some of you see it in one another, so you do not conceal yourselves from it.
And His saying: ﴿Do you indeed approach men with desire, instead of women? Rather, you are a people who are ignorant.﴾ We have already explained it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 56:

The words of the Most High: ﴿So the answer of his people was only that they said, "Expel the family of Lot from your town; indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure."﴾ This has already been explained.
Allah's statement: ﴿So We saved him and his family, except his wife; We decreed that she be among those who remained behind.﴾ That is, We made her among those who remained in the punishment.

Divine saying, the Exalted: ﴿So We rained upon them a rain, and evil was the rain of those who were warned﴾. In the narrative: the people of Lot were swallowed up by the earth, and the scattered stones were pursued from among them, so He destroyed them.

And His saying ﴿and evil was the rain of those who were warned﴾ means: wretched was the rain of those who were warned, and "those who were warned" are those who were made to fear destruction.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 59:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: Praise be to God, and peace be upon His servants whom He has chosen.﴾ As for His saying, ﴿His servants whom He has chosen﴾, there are several opinions. It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: They are the Companions of the Messenger of God. And also from him that he said: They are the community of Muhammad. And also from him that he said: They are all the believers, both the earlier and the later ones.

As for His saying, ﴿Is God better, or what they associate (with Him)?﴾, the meaning is: Is the worship of God better, or the worship of what they associate with Him? If it is said: There is no good at all in worshipping other than God, so how does the meaning of the verse hold? The answer is: They believed that there was good in it, so the verse came in accordance with that belief. Some of them said: They believed that the idols were gods, and without their belief the saying ﴿Is God better, or what they associate (with Him)?﴾ would not be sound. Sibawayh has related that the Arabs say: "O man, is wretchedness better, or happiness?" while he knows that there is no good in wretchedness and that all good is in happiness.

Hassan ibn Thabit said:

(Do you satirize him, when you are not his equal? ... So the evil of you both is a ransom for the good of you both.)

Some of them said: The meaning of ﴿Is God better, or what they associate (with Him)?﴾ is: Is the good in this, or in this which you associate with God? It is also possible that its meaning is: Is the reward of God better, or the reward of what you associate with Him?

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 60:

His saying: ﴿Is He who created the heavens and the earth and sent down for you water from the sky﴾ means: is there good in what you say and call upon of the gods, or in He who created the heavens and the earth? That is: who brought them into being.

And His saying: ﴿And sent down for you water from the sky, and We caused to grow thereby gardens full of delight﴾: every orchard enclosed by a wall is a ḥadīqah (garden). And His saying: ﴿full of delight﴾ means: having a pleasing appearance. It has also been said: al-bahjah is that in which one takes delight.

And His saying: ﴿It was not for you to make grow its trees﴾ means: it is not fitting for you to do that, because you are not able to do it.

And His saying: ﴿Is there a god with Allah?﴾ is a question in the sense of denial, meaning: there is no god with Allah.

And His saying: ﴿Nay, but they are a people who ascribe equals (to Him)﴾ means: they deviate from the truth. It has also been said: they associate with Him others, and make them equal to Him, that is, peers.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 61:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Is not He who made the earth a place of settlement﴾, meaning: a place where they may settle upon it.

And His saying: ﴿and made rivers within it﴾, meaning: within the earth.

And His saying: ﴿and made within it firm mountains﴾, meaning: mountains that are fixed.

And His saying: ﴿and made between the two seas a barrier﴾. Opinions differ regarding "the two seas." Some said: the sea of the sky and the earth. Others said: the Persian Sea and the Roman Sea. And others said: the salt sea and the fresh-water sea. As for His saying ﴿a barrier﴾, we have already explained the meaning of barrier (ḥājiz). It is said: He restrains the salt from the fresh and the fresh from the salt by His power. And this is evidence that it is permissible for Him to restrain fire from burning and a sword from cutting.

And His saying: ﴿Is there a god along with Allah?﴾ We have already explained it.

And His saying: ﴿Nay, but most of them do not know﴾, meaning: they do not know what is beneficial to them and what is harmful to them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 62:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Is He who responds to the distressed one when he calls upon Him﴾. He mentioned "the distressed one" (al-mudtarr), although He answers the supplication of the distressed and of others than the distressed; this is because the distressed person's desire (raghbah) is stronger and his supplication more humble.

His saying: ﴿and removes the evil﴾, meaning: the harm (al-durr).

His saying: ﴿and makes you successors (khulafa') of the earth﴾, meaning: He makes some of you successors of others. It has also been said: He makes your children your successors. And some of them said its meaning is: He makes you successors of the jinn on the earth.

His saying: ﴿Is there a god with Allah? Little do you take heed﴾. It has been recited as "yatadhakkarun" (with ya'), so His saying ﴿tadhakkarun﴾ is in the second-person address, and "yadhakkarun" is in the third-person (absent) form.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 27, verse 63:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Or who guides you through the darknesses of the land and the sea?﴾ That is: who guides you (yurshidukum).

And His saying: ﴿And who sends the winds as glad tidings before His mercy?﴾ That is: bringing good news (mubashshirah). It was also read as "nushran" (nashiran), that is: spreading out (nashizah).

And His saying: ﴿before His mercy﴾ means: the rain. And His saying: ﴿Is there a god with Allah? Exalted is Allah above what they associate with Him.﴾ That is: He is sanctified and exalted above what they associate with Him.

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Is it not He who originates creation and then repeats it?﴾ So His words ﴿then repeats it﴾ mean: He will restore them alive after their death.

And His words ﴿And who provides for you from the heaven and the earth?﴾ mean: from the heaven by rain, and from the earth by plants.

And His words ﴿Is there any god with Allah? Say: Produce your proof, if you should be truthful.﴾ mean: Is there another god with Allah?
His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Say: None in the heavens and the earth knows the unseen except Allah, and they do not perceive when they will be resurrected﴾. That is, when will they be raised?

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 66:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Rather, their knowledge has been overtaken concerning the Hereafter﴾. It is read also as "Bal adrak" (بل أدْرك). Some said that the two readings have the same meaning. Others said that "idarak" (ادارك) means it followed on and kept pace, and that "adrak" (أدْرك) means it reached and caught up. As for the meaning of the verse, al-Suddi said: they became knowledgeable in the Hereafter about what they did not know in this world, and this is similar in meaning to the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿How well they will hear and see﴾. Ibn Sa'id al-Darir reported: "Bal adrak" means that in the Hereafter they came to know that what they had been promised is true. This is close to the first explanation. They also recited, citing al-Akhtal:

(And my knowledge has grasped about Sawa'a that she stays upon the strings and the turbid drink)

That is: my knowledge encompassed that she was like this. Ali ibn Isa mentioned that the meaning of "bal" here is: if they had perceived in this world what they perceive in the Hereafter, they would not have doubted. Al-Farra' said: the words ﴿Rather, their knowledge has been overtaken concerning the Hereafter﴾ mean that their knowledge disappeared and fell away in this world, in the sense that they did not know. It was reported from Ibn Abbas that he read "Bala idarak" (بلَى ادارك) as an interrogative, meaning: it has not been overtaken. This supports the view of al-Farra'.

The words ﴿Rather, they are in doubt about it﴾ mean: they are in doubt about it today.

The words ﴿Rather, they are blind to it﴾ mean: they are not guided to it. It is said: the first "bal" carries the sense of "law" (if) according to what we have explained, the second "bal" carries the sense of "am" (or), and the third "bal" is in its literal sense. Some scholars mentioned that the words ﴿Rather, their knowledge has been overtaken﴾ mean: their conjecture followed on in the Hereafter, and kept pace, by speaking on the basis of guesswork and surmise.

The words ﴿Rather, they are blind to it﴾ mean: they are ignorant of the Hereafter.
Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And those who disbelieve say: "When we and our fathers have become dust, shall we indeed be brought forth?"﴾ We have already explained it.
"And His saying: ﴿We have indeed been promised this, we and our fathers before[,]﴾ up to the end of the verse, has already been discussed."
"His saying: ﴿Say: Travel through the land and see how was the end of the criminals﴾ means: of the people of Salih, the people of Lut, the companions of al-Hijr, and others."

**Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 27, verse 70:**

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not grieve over them, and do not be in distress﴾. That is: your heart should not be constricted by what they plot, and by their scheming and their deceit through falsehood.
And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they say, "When will this promise be fulfilled, if you are truthful?"﴾ That is: the Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 72:

And His saying: ﴿Say: Perhaps there has followed (radifa) for you﴾. "Radifa lakum" and "radifakum" have one meaning, and it is said: "radifa lakum" and "radifakum," meaning: it drew near to you. Abu 'Ubayda said: it came after you. Al-Qutaybi said: it followed you. From this comes "radf al-mar'a al-rajul" (the woman riding behind the man). The poet said:

(The blackness turned to whiteness at his temples... no welcome to the whiteness of grey hair when it came as a follower.)

And His saying: ﴿some of that which you are hastening﴾. It is said: it is the killing on the Day of Badr, and it is said: it is the punishment of the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 73:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is full of bounty toward mankind﴾, meaning: bounties upon mankind. And in some reports it is related that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The creation will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection, and a people will be brought forward, and it will be said to them: 'Why did you worship your Lord?' They will say: 'O Lord, You promised us Paradise, so we worshipped You out of eagerness for it and longing for it.' So He will admit them into Paradise. Then a people will be brought forward, and it will be said to them: 'Why did you worship your Lord?' They will say: 'O Lord, You frightened us of the Fire, so we worshipped You out of fear of it.' So God will save you from the Fire and admit them into Paradise. Then a people will be brought forward, and it will be said to them: 'Why did you worship your Lord?' They will say: 'Out of love for You.' So the Lord, may He be exalted, will manifest Himself to them, and they will look upon Him. That is His saying: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is full of bounty toward mankind﴾." And the report is exceedingly strange.

And His saying: ﴿But most of them do not give thanks﴾, meaning: for the blessings of God.

Qur'an 27:74: "And indeed your Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they disclose."

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed your Lord knows what their breasts conceal﴾, meaning: what their breasts hide.

And His saying: ﴿and what they disclose﴾ — its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 27, verse 75:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And there is not an unseen thing in the heaven or the earth﴾, that is: a single unseen thing from among all the unseen things. It is also said: "And there is not a hidden news."

And His saying: ﴿except that it is in a clear Book﴾ is: the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz).
Almighty God's words: ﴿Indeed, this Qur'an relates to the Children of Israel most of what they differ about﴾. That is: it makes clear to the Children of Israel most of what they differ about.

The words of God Most High: ﴿And indeed it is guidance and mercy for the believers﴾. On this there are two opinions. The first is that the pronoun refers to the Messenger, and the second is that it refers to the Qur'an.

Almighty God's words: ﴿Indeed, your Lord will judge between them by His decree﴾, meaning: He will settle the matter between them by His true judgment.

And His words: ﴿And He is the All-Mighty, the All-Knowing﴾, meaning: the Invincible in His dominion, the Knowing of the affairs of His creation.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 79:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So put your trust in Allah﴾, meaning: have confidence in Allah. ﴿Indeed, you are upon the manifest truth﴾, meaning: the manifest truth.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 80:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear﴾. What is meant by "the dead" here is: the disbelievers. This is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿[They are] dead, not alive﴾. So He called them dead because their hearts were dead; and because they did not benefit (from guidance), they became like the dead.

Some of them recited:

(You would have made [someone] hear had you called a living one... but there is no life for the one I call)

And His saying: ﴿Nor can you make the deaf hear the call﴾. It was also recited: "the deaf do not hear the call." So His saying "you cannot make hear" is addressed to the Prophet, and His saying "the deaf do not hear the call" is a statement of fact.

And His saying: ﴿when they turn away, retreating﴾, meaning: turning away. If it is asked: if they are deaf, what is the meaning of His saying ﴿when they turn away, retreating﴾? For if they are deaf, they do not hear whether they turn away retreating or not? We say: a deaf person who is present may hear if the voice is raised loudly, and may understand through some kind of gesture; but when he turns his back and retreats, he does not hear at all. It is also permissible that this mention is for the purpose of emphasis and intensification.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And you cannot guide the blind away from their straying. You can make none hear except those who believe in Our signs, so they are submitting.﴾ That is, he who comes intending belief in Our signs. It was also said: "You do not make hear except the believers."

As for His saying: ﴿so they are submitting﴾, that is, to Allah.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 82:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when the word is fulfilled against them﴾, meaning: the punishment is due upon them. Qatadah said: when Allah becomes angry with them. It is related from Ibn 'Umar: when they do not enjoin what is good and do not forbid what is evil.

And His saying: ﴿We will bring forth for them a creature from the earth﴾. It is narrated from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "It is not a creature that has a tail, but it has a beard," as if he were pointing to the fact that it is a man and not a creature. However, most scholars hold that it is a creature (dabbah), and it will emerge at the end of time.

It is said: the first of the signs of the Hour is the rising of the sun from its west and the emergence of the creature of the earth.

Ibn 'Abbas said: it has down and feathers and four legs.
