It is related from Ibn al-Zubayr that he said: "It is a creature whose head is that of an ox, whose eye is that of a pig, whose ear is that of an elephant, whose horn is that of a camel, whose neck is that of an ostrich, whose chest is that of a lion, whose hide is that of a leopard, whose flank is that of a cat, and whose legs are those of a camel; between each two of its joints is twelve cubits."

Ibn Mas'ud said: it will emerge from al-Safa, running like the gallop of a horse for three days, and only a third of it will emerge, and its head will reach the sky.

In some of the musnads it is related from the Prophet that he said: (“Evil is the valley of Jiyad.” It was said: “And why, O Messenger of Allah?” He said:) "The creature will emerge from it and will cry out three cries that will be heard by everything between the two horizons."

It is related from Hudhayfah ibn Usayd that he said: "The creature will emerge three times. It will emerge the first time in some of the valleys, then it will lie hidden, then it will emerge among the tribes of the Arabs, then it will emerge in a gathering," and he pointed out that it will emerge in the Sacred Mosque.

It is related from 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas that he ascended al-Safa and struck the stone with his staff and said: "Indeed the creature hears the sound of this staff of mine." A similar report was narrated from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr.

Hammad ibn Salamah has narrated from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Khalid ibn Aws, from Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet said: "The creature will emerge with the staff of Musa and the seal of Sulayman. It will illuminate the face of the believer and blacken the face of the disbeliever, so that people gather around a table and it says: 'This one is for that one, O disbeliever,' and it says: 'This one is for that one, O believer.'" The Shaykh, the Imam, may Allah be pleased with him, said: This report was related to us by Abu 'Abdullah 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Abdullah ibn Ahmad, who said: Abu al-'Abbas ibn Siraj related to us, who said: Abu al-'Abbas ibn Mahbub related to us, who said: Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi related to us, who said: 'Abd ibn Humayd related to us, from Rawh ibn 'Ubadah, from Hammad ibn Salamah, the hadith.

In the tafsir it is stated that the creature will mark the face of the believer with a white spot, so his face turns white by it, and it will mark the face of the disbeliever with a black spot, so his face turns black by it.

It is related from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud that he recited the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And when the word is fulfilled against them﴾, then said: "Circumambulate the House before it is lifted, recite the Qur'an before it is lifted, and say 'There is no god but Allah' before it is forgotten," then he mentioned that there will come a time when people will forget the saying "There is no god but Allah," and people will fall into the poetry of the Jahiliyyah.

His saying: ﴿speaks to them﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and 'Asim al-Jahdari recited: "tukallimuhum" (تكلمهم), meaning: they wound them. The *kalm* is the wound, and it is said: it marks them. The poet said:

((In the wounds, bowed, it denies its grammatical structure... by the deficiency of the verse, the wounds, when the complete wound...))

The well-known reading is ﴿tukallimuhum﴾ (تكلمهم). Some scholars of knowledge said: the manifestation of the verse from it is speech, and it speaks in a figurative sense, not that it actually speaks. The more correct view is that it actually speaks. The opinions differ as to what it will speak: one of the two views is that its speech is that this one is a believer and that one is a disbeliever. The other view is that it will speak with what Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿that the people were not certain of Our signs﴾.

It is read: "anna" (أن) and "inna" (إن), with the alif pronounced with a fatha and with a kasra. Whoever reads "anna" with a fatha on the alif, its meaning is "because"; whoever reads "inna" is on a fresh start (isti'naf). Ubayy ibn Ka'b read: "dabbatan tunabbi'uhum" (دابة تنبئهم), and in some readings: "tuhaddithuhum" (تحدثهم). In the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: "tukallimuhum bi-anna al-nas kanu bi-ayatina la yuqinun" (تكلمهم بأن الناس كانوا بآياتنا لا يوقنون).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 83:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And on the Day We gather from every nation a crowd﴾ mean: from every generation (qarn) a crowd. And His words: ﴿of those who deny Our signs﴾ mean: of the deniers. Here "min" (from/of) is not for partitive sense (ta'id), because all the deniers will be gathered.

And His words: ﴿then they will be driven on﴾ mean: they will be driven to the Fire. If it is said: "Do not those who are not deniers also get gathered?" We say: the gathering in which one is driven to the Fire is only for the deniers.

On the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Until, when they arrive, He will say, "Did you deny My signs while you did not comprehend them in knowledge?"﴾ That is: ignorant of the matter. And it has been said: "of the outcome of denial."

And His words: ﴿Or what was it that you used to do?﴾ is a question asked in the manner of rebuke (istifham 'ala tariq al-inkar).

God's words: "And the word will fall upon them for what they have wronged, so they will not speak." (Qur'an 27:85)

Al-Sam'ani's commentary: His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿And the word will fall upon them for what they have wronged﴾ means: the punishment became binding upon them because of what they associated with Him (in worship).

And His saying: ﴿so they will not speak﴾. Qatadah said: How could they speak when they have no proof?

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 86:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Have they not seen that We made the night for them to rest in﴾ has already been explained.

And His saying: ﴿and the day giving sight﴾ means: having sight (mubsiran dhā ibsār). The poet said:

(Kullīnī lahum [yā Umayma] nāṣib ...)

That is: possessing weariness (nāṣib dhū naṣb).

It was also said: mubsiran means "in which one sees," just as one says laylun nā'im, meaning "a night in which one sleeps." The poet said:

(Taqūlu Sulaymā lā ta'arraḍ bi-balaghatin ... wa-layluka 'an layli al-ṣa'ālīki nā'im)

That is: in which one sleeps.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe﴾ is apparent in meaning.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 87:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And the day the Horn is blown﴾ has already been explained. And His saying: ﴿So whoever is in the heavens and whoever is in the earth will be terrified﴾ means: so whoever is in the heavens and whoever is in the earth will fall unconscious (ṣa'iqa). He mentioned the terror only because it leads them to the swoon. It is said: Isrāfīl (peace be upon him) will blow three blasts: the blast of terror (nafkhat al-faza'), the blast of swooning (nafkhat al-ṣa'q), and the blast of rising for the Lord of the worlds. It has been reported that al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī said: "The Ṣūr is the Ṣūr," and some of them interpreted his words and said: "The spirits are placed in the [horn], and then it is blown into, so the spirits go to the bodies, and the bodies come to life."

And His saying: ﴿except whom Allah wills﴾ has two opinions. The first: what is meant by it is Jibrīl, Mīkā'īl, Isrāfīl and the Angel of Death, may the blessings of Allah be upon them. The other opinion: what is meant by it is the martyrs. In some reports: "The martyrs are the exception of Allah," i.e., those whom Allah, exalted is He, has excepted. The exception applies to them because they are alive, as Allah, exalted is He, said. And in some traditions: "They are alive, bearing swords, circling around the Throne."

And His saying: ﴿and all will come to Him humbled﴾ means: abased (ṣāghirīn). It was also read: "wa-kullun atawhu" in the past tense, and the meaning is close.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 88:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And you see the mountains, you think them solid, [but] they pass by like the passing of clouds﴾. That is: standing still.

And His words: ﴿and they pass by like the passing of clouds﴾. That is: they move the way clouds move. This is because the movement of clouds is not seen due to their vastness; likewise, the movement of the mountains on the Day of Resurrection will not be seen due to their multitude. The poet said: (With a host as huge as a mountain, you think them ... standing still for the pilgrims, while the riding-camels are trotting).

That is: they are trotting (tahamlaja).

And His words: ﴿The handiwork of God, who has perfected everything﴾. That is: He has made everything firm and sound.

And His words: ﴿Indeed, He is Aware of what you do﴾. That is: of what you make (taṣna'ūn).

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Whoever comes with a good deed, for him there is better than it﴾. That is, for him there is good from it. Some of them said: for him there is good that reaches him from it. Among them is one who said: "better than it" means more beneficial than it. As for the good deed (al-hasanah), according to the view of the majority of the commentators (al-mufassirun), it is the statement "There is no god but Allah" (la ilaha illa Allah). It was also said: it is every act of obedience. And it is related from Abu Dharr that he was asked, and it was said to him: "Is the statement 'There is no god but Allah' a good deed?" He said: "It is the best of good deeds."

And His words: ﴿and they will be secure from the terror of that Day﴾. We have already explained the meaning of al-fazaʿ (terror) earlier. It has been recited as "fazaʿun yawmaʾidhin" with an idafah (construct form), and it has been recited as "fazaʿun yawmaʾidhin" with tanwin (nunation). Abu ʿAli al-Farisi said: "fazaʿun yawmaʾidhin" with tanwin indicates intensification (al-takthir), whereas "fazaʿi yawmaʾidhin" with the idafah does not indicate intensification.

**Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 90:**

Allah's words: ﴿And whoever comes with an evil deed, their faces will be thrown into the Fire﴾, and His words: ﴿Are you recompensed except for what you used to do?﴾ — their meaning is apparent.

Some of them said concerning His words ﴿better than it﴾: He only said this because the reward for good deeds is multiplied, namely that it reaches ten times and more. So His words ﴿better than it﴾ mean: more than it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 91:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, I have been commanded to worship the Lord of this city, who has made it sacred﴾. Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn 'Abbas recited: "allati harramaha" (the one which He has made sacred). So His saying ﴿allati harramaha﴾ refers to the city (al-balda). (His saying ﴿alladhi﴾ refers to God, and this is well known. As for the sanctification (tahrim), it is the sanctification of hunting, and it was what we mentioned earlier.)

And His saying: ﴿And to Him belongs everything﴾, meaning: and everything belongs to God. And His saying: ﴿And I have been commanded to be among the Muslims﴾, meaning: among those who submit to God.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 27, verse 92:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And that I should recite the Qur'an﴾, meaning: "And I have been commanded to recite the Qur'an." The scholars (ahl al-'ilm) said: "[It means] to recite it and act upon it." It is narrated from al-Hasan al-Basri, who said: "The people were commanded to act upon the Qur'an, but they made its recitation (tilawah) into an action."

And His words: ﴿Whoever is guided, then he is only guided for [the benefit of] his own self﴾, meaning: the benefit of his being guided returns to himself.

And His words: ﴿And whoever goes astray, say, "I am only one of the warners."﴾, meaning: the ones who warn (al-mukhawwifin).

The Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 27, verse 93:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And say: "All praise is due to Allah."﴾ This is an address to the Prophet and to all the believers.

And His words: ﴿He will show you His signs﴾, meaning: His indications (dalalat).

And His words: ﴿so you will recognize them﴾, meaning: you will recognize the indications.

And His words: ﴿And your Lord is not unaware of what you do﴾, its meaning is apparent.

A report has come concerning the preceding verse, which is His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Whoever comes with a good deed﴾. Most of the exegetes hold that what is meant by the good deed is faith (iman), and by the bad deed is polytheism (shirk). Safwan ibn 'Assal al-Muradi narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "On the Day of Resurrection, faith and polytheism will come. They will kneel before the Most Merciful, and each of them will claim its people. Allah, may He be exalted, will say to faith: 'Go with your people to Paradise.' And Allah, may He be exalted, will say to polytheism: 'Go with your people to the Fire.'" Then he recited His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Whoever comes with a good deed will have better than it﴾, to the end of the verse. The report is gharib (rare, with a weak or singular chain), and Allah knows best.
